title: Output contract introspection and parse-error UX improvements for streaming tool-calls
author: Maya Alvarez
release_notes: Added response_format=diagnostic for human-friendly parse errors and streaming resume tokens; improved OpenAI function_call mapping for partial/repairable JSON in streams.
description:
Motivation: Customers using strict schema enforcement + streaming tool-calls have been hit by opaque parse errors when the model emits slightly malformed JSON mid-stream. This causes poor UX for manual debugging and complicates programmatic retries. This PR introduces a diagnostics-first mode and better parse-error envelopes in the streaming path, plus small OpenAI-compat mapping changes to make function_call recovery more predictable.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a new response_format mode: "diagnostic". When set, the runtime will emit a structured but human-readable parse-diagnostic envelope on schema failures that includes: error_location (path & token index), problem_summary, suggested_repair (a short textual hint), and a resume_token that can be used with the stream resume API.
- Introduces streaming parse checkpoints: lightweight, idempotent resume tokens produced at schema-safe checkpoints so clients can re-request the subsequent token window rather than re-running the whole request.
- Soft-repair hinting: when the runtime detects common structural mistakes (trailing commas, unclosed arrays/objects, truncated strings) it returns a suggested_repair string and a sample corrected fragment to aid tooling and UIs.
- Tool-call/Function-call fence updates: for OpenAI-compat function_call behavior we now emit an explicit "tool_fence" envelope before a tool invocation and a "tool_result" envelope on completion. If the stream contains parseable-but-incomplete arguments for a tool, the runtime uses the resume_token mechanism instead of immediately failing the entire response.
- Maintains backward compatibility: default behavior remains unchanged; diagnostic envelopes are opt-in via response_format=diagnostic or the new SDK flag ResponseOptions.diagnostic=true.

Commits (high level):
- feat(api): introduce diagnostic response_format (Maya Alvarez)
- feat(runtime): streaming checkpoint manager + resume token generation (E. Harris)
- fix(stream): map incomplete function_call args to resume flow instead of hard fail (Priya Shah)
- test: add integration tests for resume tokens and repair suggestions (Liam O'Connor)
- docs: explain diagnostic mode and migration notes (Maya Alvarez)

Files touched (high-level):
- runtime/stream/checkpoint_manager.rs  (new) — checkpointing & token anchors
- runtime/contract/diagnostic_formatter.go (new) — human-friendly error envelopes
- api/handlers/generate_handler.py — plumbs response_format param and resume headers
- openai_compat/adapter.ts — emits tool_fence/tool_result envelopes and maps function_call recovery

CI & tests:
- First CI run failed due to a flaky resume token race in checkpoint_manager; fixed by serializing resume token writes and added a unit test. Reran CI; all checks now pass (unit, integration, linters).

Reviewer notes / tradeoffs:
- Performance: checkpointing adds a trivial memory overhead (anchors stored per-request) but keeps token emission hot-path fast; benchmarks show <2% p99 latency impact for common workloads.
- Security: resume tokens are short-lived (TTL=2m) and opaque; no sensitive data is encoded. We added an audit log entry for resume token issuance for enterprise traceability.
- UX: The suggested_repair is intentionally conservative (short hint + sample fragment) to avoid leaking model hallucinations into automated repair flows. The runtime will never auto-apply repairs — reconstruction is left to the caller.

Migration / rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind ResponseOptions.diagnostic and a server-side feature flag. We will enable for 10% of host customers initially and onboard specific enterprise beta customers via opt-in.
- Docs and SDK updates shipped together: python & ts SDKs add a ResponseOptions.diagnostic flag and examples.

Testing & QA notes:
- Added targeted unit tests for the diagnostic formatter including edge cases: nested arrays, truncated binary-like strings, and tool-call arg truncation.
- Integration tests cover resume token correctness across a simulated network reconnect.
- Manual QA: exercised the diagnostic UI demo with various malformed token sequences and validated repair suggestions produced actionable hints 84% of the time (internal QA metric).

Review thread (highlights):
- Jonas Wu: "Nice UX improvement. Please ensure resume tokens are invalidated on model/context-change."
  - Author reply: "Added invalidation on model switch and included an audit entry — see checkpoint_manager.rs."
- Priya Shah: "Can we avoid any automatic repair?"
  - Author reply: "Confirmed: suggestions only; no auto-apply. Documented in response_format.md."

Merge: Squash and merge. Merged after 2 approvals.

Notes for support/SEs:
- When a customer sees a "diagnostic" envelope, they should present the suggested_repair and offer a "Retry from here" button wired to resume_token. Example header returned: X-Resume-Token: <opaque-token> and a JSON envelope in-stream of type: "diagnostic/parse_error".
